title: O, Heaven Is Where No Secret Dread
description: O, Heaven Is Where No Secret Dread in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 361, “A Vision of Heaven”, where the book credits them to Briggs' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, heaven is where no se-cret dread May haunt us by its power; Where from the past no gloom is shed Up-on the pre-sent hour.

lines: O, heaven is where no secret dread
May haunt us by its power;
Where from the past no gloom is shed
And there the living waters flow
The soul, now wandering here, shall know
The burden of the stranger's heart,
And, borne on eagle's wings afar,
Free thought shall claim its dower,
From every sphere, from every star,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
